In [[abstract algebra]], a '''Robbins algebra''' is an [[Universal algebra#Basic idea|algebra]] containing a single [[binary operation]] <math>\lor</math> and a single [[unary operation]] <math>\neg</math> that satisfy the following [[Universal algebra#Equations|axioms]]:<ref name=":0">{{cite web |last1=Weisstein |first1=Eric W. |title=Robbins Algebra |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/RobbinsAlgebra.html |access-date=2025-09-09}}</ref>

For all elements ''a'', ''b'', and ''c'':
# [[Associativity]]: <math>a \lor \left(b \lor c \right) = \left(a \lor b \right) \lor c</math>
# [[Commutativity]]: <math>a \lor b = b \lor a</math>
# ''Robbins equation'': <math>\neg \left( \neg \left(a \lor b \right) \lor \neg \left(a \lor \neg b \right) \right) = a</math>

For many years, it was conjectured, but unproven, that all Robbins algebras are [[Boolean algebra (structure)|Boolean algebra]]s. This was proved by [[William McCune]] in 1997,<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=McCune |first1=William |date=1997 |title=Solution of the Robbins Problem |journal=Journal of Automated Reasoning |volume=19 |issue=3 |pages=263–276 |doi=10.1023/A:1005843212881 }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Dahn |first=Bernd I |date=1998-10-15 |title=Robbins Algebras Are Boolean: A Revision of McCune's Computer-Generated Solution of Robbins Problem |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0021869398974671 |journal=Journal of Algebra |volume=208 |issue=2 |pages=526–532 |doi=10.1006/jabr.1998.7467 |issn=0021-8693|url-access=subscription }}</ref> so the term "Robbins algebra" is now simply a synonym for "Boolean algebra".

== History<!--'Robbins conjecture' redirects here-->==
In 1933, [[Edward Huntington]] proposed a new set of axioms for Boolean algebras,<ref>{{cite journal |last=Huntington |first=Edward V. |title=New sets of independent postulates for the algebra of logic, with special reference to Whitehead and Russell's Principia mathematica |journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society |date=1933 |volume=35 |pages=274–304 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-1933-1501684-X |doi-access=free |jstor=1989325}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Huntington |first1=Edward V. |title=Boolean algebra. A correction|journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society |date=1933 |volume=35 |issue=2 |pages=557–558 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-1933-1501702-9 |doi-access=free |jstor=1989783}}</ref> consisting of (1) and (2) above, plus: 
*''Huntington's equation'': <math>\neg(\neg a \lor b) \lor \neg(\neg a \lor \neg b) = a.</math>
From these axioms, Huntington derived the usual axioms of Boolean algebra.

Very soon thereafter, [[Herbert Robbins]] posed the '''Robbins conjecture'''<!--boldface per WP:R#PLA-->, namely that the Huntington equation could be replaced with what came to be called the Robbins equation, and the result would still be [[Boolean algebra (structure)|Boolean algebra]]. <math>\lor</math> would interpret Boolean [[Boolean algebra (structure)#Definition|join]] and <math>\neg</math> Boolean [[Boolean algebra (structure)#Definition|complement]]. Boolean [[Boolean algebra (structure)#Definition|meet]] and the constants 0 and 1 are easily defined from the Robbins algebra primitives. Pending verification of the conjecture, the system of Robbins was called "Robbins algebra".

Verifying the Robbins conjecture required proving Huntington's equation, or some other axiomatization of a Boolean algebra, as theorems of a Robbins algebra. Huntington, Robbins, [[Alfred Tarski]], and others worked on the problem, but failed to find a proof or counterexample.

===McCune's proof===

In 1996, [[William McCune]] proved the conjecture using the [[automated theorem proving|automated theorem prover]] EQP (equational prover).<ref name="proof">{{cite journal |last1=McCune |first1=William |date=1996 |title=Robbins algebras are boolean |url=https://calculemus.org/MathUniversalis/4/6robbins.html |journal=Association for Automated Reasoning Newsletter |volume=35 |pages=1–3}}</ref> EQP was developed by McCune while working at the Mathematics and Computer Science Division of the [[Argonne National Laboratory]].<ref name="NYT">{{cite news |last1=Kolata |first1=Gina |title=Computer Math Proof Shows Reasoning Power |url=https://archive.nytimes.com/www.nytimes.com/library/cyber/week/1210math.html |access-date=10 December 2025 |work=The New York Times |date=December 10, 1996}}</ref> McCune considered EQP a prototype which he developed specifically to prove the Robbins conjecture, unlike [[Otter (theorem prover)|OTTER]], another theorem prover which he developed for general use.<ref name="In memory">{{cite book |editor-last1=Bonacina |editor-first1=Maria Paola |editor-last2=Stickel |editor-first2=Mark E. |title=Automated Reasoning and Mathematics: Essays in Memory of William W. McCune |date=2013 |publisher=Springer |location=Berlin, Heidelberg |isbn=3642366740 |page=IX |url=https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/bfm:978-3-642-36675-8/1#page=7 |access-date=10 December 2025}}</ref> The proof took eight days to be completed by EQP. McCune later called Robbins, then 81 years old, to tell him that the conjecture had been proved.<ref name="NYT"/>

McCune's proof built on prior work on the conjecture by Steve Winker, also a researcher at Argonne.<ref name="proof"/><ref name="legacy">{{cite book|last=Wos|first=Larry|chapter=The Legacy of a Great Researcher |editor-last1=Bonacina |editor-first1=Maria Paola |editor-last2=Stickel |editor-first2=Mark E. |title=Automated Reasoning and Mathematics: Essays in Memory of William W. McCune |date=2013 |publisher=Springer |location=Berlin, Heidelberg |isbn=3642366740 |page=6 |url=https://www.mcs.anl.gov/uploads/cels/papers/P4009-1212.pdf |access-date=10 December 2025}}</ref>

For a complete proof of the Robbins conjecture in one consistent notation and following McCune closely, see Mann (2003).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Wampler-Doty |first1=Matthew |date=2010 |title=A complete proof of the Robbins conjecture |url=http://afp.sf.net/entries/Robbins-Conjecture.shtml |journal=The Archive of Formal Proofs.}}</ref> Dahn (1998) simplified McCune's machine proof.<ref name=":1" />
